learning_outcomes.text: Know, understand, and apply computer tools for design, analysis, and manufacturing for the development of tools for mass production, providing great flexibility to adapt to new situations.
Analyze the manufacturing problem qualitatively and quantitatively, proposing manufacturing solutions using methods and technologies in the field of industrial engineering.

Adequately communicate knowledge, procedures, results, skills, and aspects of the mass production technological process in the field of Industrial Engineering, using appropriate vocabulary, specific terminology, and means.

Work effectively in multidisciplinary and multilingual environments, integrating capabilities and knowledge to make decisions related to the manufacturing process in the field of industrial engineering.

syllabus_topics: Metal molds for injection molded plastic parts.
Analysis and simulation of the injection process (CAE).
Tools for mold design and manufacturing (CAD_CAM).
Dies, stamps, and matrices for plastic forming of sheet metal.
Analysis and simulation of the stamping process (CAE).
Tools for the design and manufacturing of dies and matrices (CAD_CAM).
Tools for mold and die manufacturing and their application.
assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, the final grade is based on a written or oral exam (70%) and individual assignments (30%). However, students who attend at least 80% of classes and satisfactorily complete assignments will have their practical grade added to the exam grade; otherwise, only the exam grade will count (100%). The regulations governing student assessment for official Bachelor's degrees will apply. In the extraordinary call, a single final test or exam covering all course content will be conducted.
